title: OpenAI autolog stream hook must bind loop variable before the loop for zero-chunk streams
answers: UnboundLocalError chunk when OpenAI streaming response is empty with autolog
openai autolog streaming call crashes when the stream ends with no chunks
stream ends immediately with data: [DONE] and mlflow autolog raises
mlflow openai autolog empty streaming response trace outputs none
body:
Symptom: With mlflow.openai.autolog() on, a streaming chat completion that ends without sending any chunk (server sends data: [DONE] right away) raises UnboundLocalError: chunk when the stream ends, so the user's loop fails even though the API call succeeded.
Root cause: mlflow/openai/autolog.py:_stream_output_logging_hook (sync and async variants) reads the loop variable `chunk` after the for/async for loop; if the stream yields zero items, the name is never bound.
Fix pattern: initialize `chunk = None` before the loop in both sync and async hooks, so the post-loop code (_process_last_chunk) runs with outputs=None and the span ends normally.
Constraints: Applies to any post-loop code that reads a loop variable in these hooks. Does not cover exceptions raised mid-stream, which are handled separately. Keep the sync and async hooks in parity when editing either.
applies: OpenAI autolog streaming hooks in mlflow/openai/autolog.py (Chat Completions and Responses API share the hook).
says: Streaming model responses that return no content crash the application when tracing is enabled.
Empty streaming chat completions fail with an internal error when autologging is turned on.
Streaming calls should finish successfully even when the model returns zero output tokens.
Tracing crashes if a streaming chat response ends immediately without emitting any chunks.
Allow zero-token streaming responses to complete without failing the consumer loop.
search: In OpenAI autolog streaming hooks for Chat Completions and Responses API, the stream loop variable chunk must be initialized to None before the loop. This prevents UnboundLocalError when a stream ends with zero chunks, allowing post-loop code in _process_last_chunk to run with outputs=None and end the span normally. Enforced in both sync and async variants of _stream_output_logging_hook in mlflow/openai/autolog.py, which must maintain parity and do not handle mid-stream exceptions.
